messages:
amanda: Quick sync — ArgoBank wants a short POC to prove we can accept VectorServe-style requests and get prompt parity. They asked: can we do a drop-in adapter + dedicated instance? timeline: 2 weeks. 
ryan: @amanda yep. We can implement a lightweight adapter that maps VectorServe API->Redwood. Biggest risk: response-format differences (metadata fields + stop-token behavior).
ryan: rough plan: 1) shim that translates /generate and /chat calls, 2) run prompt-parity harness (100 prompts), 3) surface diffs + mitigations.
amanda: customer asked about pricing for Dedicated during POC and production. They expect cost predictability. Any quick estimate?
ryan: quick math — POC (dedicated small pool, 2 gpus) est ~$6k/week including reserved + bandwidth. Production depends on QPS; give them committed baseline + burst. I'll draft numbers.
tess: infra note — if they want VPC Private + KMS, provisioning lead time = ~5 business days after signed order. For a POC we can do dedicated in our shared tenancy but isolate logs and use customer project. If they require VPC for even POC, we need infra ticket now.
omar: Security checklist: they sent an initial vendor questionnaire (SaaS risk). Need SOC2 report, data retention policy, KMS/HSM details, subprocessor list, and an export of audit logs for the dedicated instance. I can own the responses but will need sample contract + customer's legal contact. ETA 3 business days if docs are ready.
kirill: For prompt parity I can run our eval harness. Suggest sampling across: short completions, multi-turn chat, instruction-following, and numeric extraction. We'll produce a "delta" report with: token-level BLEU-ish, hallucination count, and prompt-to-prompt variance.
amanda: great. Customer also asked about small behavioral differences: e.g., VectorServe returns `finish_reason` of "length" vs our "stop"; they use that to trigger downstream logic. Can we map that?
ryan: yes — adapter will translate finish_reason fields. Also watch for subtle temperature/penalty defaults. Recommend we set explicit model params in shim to match VectorServe defaults.
ryan: example adapter snippet (bash):
```bash
# VectorServe style request
curl -X POST https://api.vectorserve.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <VS>' -d '{"prompt":"Summarize x","max_tokens":120}'

# Redwood equivalent inside adapter
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \n  -d '{"input":"Summarize x","max_new_tokens":120,"stop":["\n\n"]}'
```
kirill: nice, I'll add that to the test harness so we compare normalized outputs.
amanda: also, sales/legal asked: any export controls or data residency blockers for EU banking?
omar: We have EU regions and can provision a Dedicated cluster in eu-west-1. Data residency: logs/audit + model telemetry can be configured not to leave the region, but customer will want proof. I can provide an architecture diagram + statement.
ryan: operational note — if parity diffs are >5% on our scoring metric we should propose a model variant or small prompt-template change. My SLA proposal: canary for 24h then full cutover.
amanda: timeline check — 2-week POC. Week1: adapter + infra + run 100-prompt parity. Week2: fix diffs, security Qs, demo. Ok?
tess: works for infra if we choose shared-tenant dedicated. If VPC required, flip week0 (prep) and extend by 5 days.
omar: I'll start the questionnaire draft now; pls DM me sample contract and the customer's security contact (legal@argobank).
kirill: I'll spin up the harness and queue the 100 prompts. Need a sample of the customer's existing prompts and a small dataset of failing cases they care about.
amanda: I'll get customer's prompt dump and legal contact. Thanks all.
deploy-bot: Deployment pipeline queued: adapter-prototype branch -> staging. CI: 8/8 checks passed.
ryan: action items: (1) amanda: collect customer's prompt set + legal contact, (2) tess: confirm infra mode (VPC vs shared), (3) omar: draft security answers, (4) kirill: run parity harness and report. We'll touch base EOD tomorrow.
amanda: thanks team :thumbsup:
